business_problem: SensoRy AI needed to convert complex wildfire sensor readings into clear, immediate guidance for responders because detecting a fire is only useful if firefighters and officials can understand the situation quickly enough to act.
solution_summary: SensoRy AI combines a solar-powered wildfire sensor network with ChatGPT so raw detections become responder-ready intelligence instead of opaque telemetry. Its field sensors watch for heat, smoke, flame, and plume activity at ignition and pass those signals through a mesh network, along with supporting context such as thermal imagery, GPS coordinates, wind conditions, and projected fire spread. ChatGPT then translates that live sensor stream into plain-language alerts that firefighters and officials can understand immediately, and Ryan Honary also built a walkie-talkie style interface so responders can ask follow-up questions such as whether a detection is a fire, where it is located, or which evacuation route is best. Voice interactions let him run tests hands-free in the field while the same model layer keeps formatting answers for operational use. The result is a system where AI sits between the raw sensor mesh and emergency decision-making.

business_outcome: SensoRy AI made wildfire alerts easier to interpret, gave responders interactive answers in seconds, and created a workflow that helps officials react sooner and with better situational clarity.
